Sandeep vs State Of Rajasthan (2025:Rj-Jd:13243) on 10 March,
2025

Author: Kuldeep Mathur Bench: Kuldeep Mathur [2025:RJ-JD:13243]
 HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN AT  JODHPUR  S.B. Criminal Appeal (Sb) No. 1795/2024 Sandeep S/o Manphool, Aged About 20 Years, R/o Gomanwali,
P.s. Ramsinghpur, Dist. Anoopgarh (Presently Lodged In Central Jail, Sriganganagar)
 ----Appellant  Versus 1. State Of Rajasthan, Through Pp 2. Manju D/o Maniram, R/o Near Durga Mandir, Vinoba Basti  Park Sriganganagar  ----Respondents For Appellant(s) : Mr. Umesh Kant Vyas For Respondent(s) : Mr. Prem Singh Panwar, PP  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KULDEEP MATHUR Order 10/03/2025 The instant appeal has been filed under Section 14-A SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act on behalf of the appellant, who is in custody in connection with F.I.R. No.336/2024,
registered at Police Station Kotwali Sriganganagar, District Sriganganagar, for the offences under Sections 376(2)(n), 341, 450, 354(d), 354(a) & 506 of IPC and Section 3(1)(r)(s)(w) & 3(2)(va) of the SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act against the order dated 18.10.2024 passed by the learned Special Judge, Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act Cases,
Sriganganagar in Criminal Bail Application No.471/2024 (CIS No.350/24), whereby, the bail application preferred under Section 483 BNSS on behalf of the appellant was rejected.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Drawing attention of the Court towards the FIR and the statements of the victim 'M' recorded under various sections of Cr.P.C., learned counsel for the appellant submitted that [2025:RJ-JD:13243] (2 of 3) [CRLAS-1795/2024] admittedly victim 'M' was having old acquaintance with the appellant.

Learned counsel further submitted that victim 'M' victim was having mutual relationship with the appellant, however, on relations between them turning sour, the victim 'M', for the alleged incident which occurred in the year 2020-21, has lodged the present FIR after a delay of about two years and falsely implicated the appellant in the present case.

Learned counsel submitted that no obscene videos and photographs of the victim 'M' allegedly used by the appellant to threatened and Sandeep vs State Of Rajasthan (2025:Rj-Jd:13243) on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88505821/
1 blackmail her have been recovered by the investigating agency.
Learned counsel submitted that as a matter of fact the appellant has not even been charge- sheeted for the offences under Information Technology Act, 2000.

Learned counsel submitted that the appellant, who is aged about 20 years, is in judicial custody and the trial of the case will take sufficiently long time to be concluded, therefore,
the benefit of bail may be granted to the accused-appellant.
Heard learned counsel for the parties at Bar and perused the material available on record.
Learned Public Prosecutor has vehemently opposed the prayer for bail.

Having regard to the entirety of facts and circumstances of the case and material available on record, this Court prima facie finds that no plausible explanation has been furnished by the victim 'M' for lodging the FIR after a delay of about two years .

This Court also prima facie finds that no obscene videos and photographs of the victim 'M' allegedly used by the appellant to threatened and blackmail her have been recovered by the investigating agency [2025:RJ-JD:13243] (3 of 3)
[CRLAS-1795/2024
] and the appellant has not even been charge-sheeted for the offences under Information Technology Act, 2000.

This Court also prima facie finds that the statements of the victim 'M' have already been recorded before the competent Criminal Court as PW-1 and the prosecution has not shown any apprehension of the petitioner influencing the prosecution witnesses of the case or fleeing away from justice, in case, he is enlarged on bail.
This Court, thus, is of the opinion that the order rejecting the application for bail filed on behalf of the appellant, cannot be sustained and deserves to be set aside.
Consequently, the instant appeal is allowed.

The impugned order dated 18.10.2024 passed by the learned Special Judge, Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act Cases,
Sriganganagar is set aside.

sentences.text:
It is ordered that the accused- appellant Sandeep S/o Manphool arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.336/2024, registered at Police Station Kotwali Sriganganagar, District Sriganganagar shall be released on bail; provided he furnishes a personal bond of Rs. 50,000/- and two surety bonds of Rs. 25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the learned trial Court with the stipulation to appear before that Court on all dates of hearing and as and when called upon to do so.
(KULDEEP MATHUR),J 170-mohit/-
